title: Streaming Horizon Concierge: latency-aware batcher with KV affinity for streaming chat
creator: Marco Geller
description: Design and implement a new batch formation heuristic ("Streaming Horizon Concierge") targeted at sustained low-latency streaming chat completions. The heuristic will balance three concerns: minimize tail latency for streaming clients, maximize KV cache locality to avoid expensive reloads, and bound GPU memory headroom to prevent OOMs during high-concurrency ramps. This ticket covers design, prototype, microbenchmarks, and a staged rollout to canary hosts.
proposal: Overview: Introduce a horizon-aware batching layer that forms 'concierge' micro-batches per active session horizon. Each concierge batch groups tokens that are likely to reuse the same KV slots and are expected to finish within a short time window to enable efficient streaming flushes.

Key heuristics: 1) Horizon TTL: assign a short lifetime (e.g., 120ms) to open horizons; if additional tokens from same session arrive within TTL, they join the concierge batch. 2) KV affinity scoring: compute affinity = f(session_recent_kv_slots, remaining_seq_len) and prefer co-locating high-affinity requests to the same GPU slab to reduce KV load. 3) Latency buckets: prioritize building batches that keep predicted tail latency below configured SLO (streaming-target-ms). 4) GPU headroom guardrail: when free GPU memory < threshold, reduce batch coalescing aggressiveness and fall back to minimal micro-batches with KV prefetch disabled where necessary.

Data inputs used: per-request estimated generation length, session last-access timestamp, session KV hotness score (eviction frequency + recency), client priority flag, and current GPU slab utilization metrics.

Implementation plan: a) scheduler-level changes to support horizon timers and per-session concierge queues; b) KV manager hook to expose slot-affinity hints to scheduler; c) runtime guardrail that monitors slab free bytes and adjusts coalescing parameters; d) telemetry hooks for per-batch KV hits/misses, latency percentiles, and memory deltas.

Trade-offs: Increased scheduler complexity and metadata overhead per session vs reduced KV reloads and lower tail latency for streaming flows. Potentially reduced throughput in severe memory pressure scenarios due to conservative batching.
Compatibility: Should integrate with existing streaming path and fall back to legacy batcher when disabled via feature flag.
Feature flags: runtime.concierge_batcher.enabled (global), runtime.concierge_batcher.kv_affinity (toggle affinity scoring), runtime.concierge_batcher.memory_guard (toggle headroom adjustments).
Success metrics: 95th and 99th percentile streaming token latency reduction, KV miss rate per slab, and GPU memory OOM incidence rate.
experiments: Experiment A: Ablation of KV affinity: compare baseline scheduler vs concierge with affinity disabled to measure contribution of affinity scoring to KV miss rate.
Experiment B: Horizon TTL sweep: evaluate TTL in [40ms, 80ms, 120ms, 250ms] to find knee between latency and batching efficiency.
Experiment C: Memory guard thresholds: simulate slab pressure and test guard thresholds at 10%, 15%, 20% free memory to measure safe operational point.
Instrument: microbench harness with synthetic conversational load (mix of short chit-chat and long multi-turn assistant sessions), and replay of production trace for two peak days.
Datasets: production trace anonymized session lengths, synthetic adversarial KV churn workloads, and unit tests for KV hint propagation.
perf_targets: Latency: 95th percentile token-to-token latency <= 120ms for streaming path under normal load (70th percentile load), and 99th <= 300ms.
KV efficiency: reduce KV reloads per session by >= 30% vs baseline for multi-turn sessions > 8 turns.
Memory: keep GPU free memory headroom >= 12% on average across canary hosts; no OOMs during 1h soak at target concurrency.
Throughput: throughput drop <= 7% relative to baseline when memory guard triggers (acceptable tradeoff).
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Local dev: unit tests + integration test using qemu-like runtime, validate correctness and feature flags.
Stage 1 - Benchmark lab: run microbench harness across all slab sizes and record KV hit/miss and latency metrics.
Stage 2 - Canary (5% hosts): enable runtime.concierge_batcher.enabled=false by default; enable on canary hosts with kv_affinity and memory_guard true; 48h soak and performance regression checks.
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: if canary is green, ramp to 25% then 60% then 100% over multiple days with monitoring alerts on SLO violations.

Rollback criteria: any increase of 99th percentile token latency > 30% or any OOM occurrence traced to new scheduler behavior triggers immediate rollback to previous scheduler and creates incident postmortem.
Communication: announce to platform channels, update runtime release notes and console feature toggles documentation.
risks_mitigation: Risk: KV affinity scoring might concentrate sessions unevenly and cause hot slab contention. Mitigation: implement probabilistic spread factor and slab load balancer feedback to divert affinity when slab load > threshold.
Risk: Scheduler metadata overhead increases per-session memory. Mitigation: compact horizon metadata into a single 64-bit token and garbage collect inactive horizons aggressively (>5s idle).
Risk: Incorrect affinity hints lead to stale KV reads. Mitigation: handshake protocol between KV manager and scheduler with a versioned hint and fallback path on mismatch.
Risk: Latency regression for short-turn sessions due to waiting TTL. Mitigation: early flush paths when predicted remaining length is zero or client requested immediate partial.
Risk: Complexity causing maintainability issues. Mitigation: document design, add observability, and limit heuristic surface via feature flags.
